title: Customer GPU Supply Bridge Planner - Sep 2027
summary: Per-contract reservation planner designed to bridge short-term spikes and long-term entitlements. Includes regional fallback slices, canary allocations, and utilization projections used by Capacity Ops for Q3-Q4 planning.

CALCULATION_NOTES:
- Allocation heuristic (per week): reserve_base = min(Reserved_GPUs, ceil(Avg_Weekday_Util% * Reserved_GPUs / 100 * safety_factor)) where safety_factor = 1.08 for enterprise, 1.15 for premium, 1.25 for startup/trial.
- Short-term spike buffer: if Peak_Observed_24h% > 1.25 * Avg_Weekday_Util%, allocate buffer = ceil(0.12 * Reserved_GPUs) up to max 12 GPUs.
- Canary sizing: min(ceil(0.06 * Reserved_GPUs), 8) but not less than 2 for enterprise customers.

FALLBACK_POLICIES_SUMMARY:
- Tier mapping: enterprise -> primary always; premium -> primary preferred + fallback with 30% throttling; standard -> fallback allowed after 6 minutes; startup/trial -> fallback allowed but billed separately.
- Cross-region KV warming: When invoking fallback, system will replay last 10k tokens of active KV prefixes to the fallback region for first 3 minutes; measure cold-start latency delta and abort fallback if > 350ms increase.

OPERATIONAL_RUNBOOK_SNIPPETS:
- To reassign 8 GPUs from low-util to high-util contract: open capacity-ops dashboard -> Select donor contract -> choose slice -> hit 'Transfer' -> add change event in changelog (MR: gitlab.com/redwood/infrastructure/-/merge_requests/412).
- Canary flow: allocate canary GPUs, deploy model variant, run 1000 sample prompts from contract's eval set, compare quality/regression metrics, then scale to full reservation if pass thresholds.
